rows.description: My friend has a costly toy and I want one too. I feel a sting and say "my parents are poor" or "my toy is better". A wise parent says "we each have different things, and we have enough". Comparing starts young.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, curiosity, fairness, pride
related mind states: envy

rows.description: My sister got more pocket money and I cry. I need fairness to be clear. A wise family explains with age-based rules and lets each child choose how to spend or save. Secret favouritism causes hidden hurt.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, curiosity, envy, pride
related mind states: sadness, hurt

rows.description: Papa helps me with my buttons and I say "thank you". I feel loved and a bit proud to be learning. Wise adults help just enough so I can finish myself, and I learn that needing help is normal.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: dependence, indebtedness
related mind states: affection, gratitude, pride

rows.description: My big brother helps with my bag and says "you owe me a sweet". I feel unsure. Wise families let older siblings help for love, without bargaining. I learn to say thanks and to help back in my own time.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: dependence, gratitude
related mind states: affection, gratitude

rows.description: An aunty picks up my dropped things and I say thank you shyly. I feel warm and surprised at her kindness. I learn that many people are kind and that thanking them makes both of us feel good.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: dependence, indebtedness
related mind states: gratitude, anger, shyness, surprise

rows.description: I keep asking the teacher to do it for me because I fear failing. I want to be safe. A wise teacher says "try one step and I will be here". Too much help stops me learning, and too little scares me.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: gratitude, indebtedness
related mind states: fear, trust

rows.description: My friend fell and I help him up and ask "are you okay?" I feel a warm ache for him. Wise adults notice and say "that was kind". A child who cares about others is learning to read feelings.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: gratitude, pride
related mind states: empathy

rows.description: My friend helped me find my lost shoe and I feel relieved and happy. I say "thank you". Being helped by a peer teaches that friends look out for each other, and I plan to help back.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, pride
related mind states: joy, gratitude, relief

rows.description: My parent notices I helped set the table and says "thank you, that was a big help". I feel important. Small chores with real thanks build a sense of being useful, without turning help into payment.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, gratitude
related mind states: gratitude, pride

rows.description: I help so the teacher will praise me. I feel happy when she notices. Mixed motives are normal at this age. A wise teacher praises the kindness itself so the child begins to help even when nobody sees.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, gratitude, pride
related mind states: joy
